data.body_html:
Choosing between the Mangusta 80 and the Ferretti 94 for your Marbella charter comes down to one question: do you want speed or space? Both boats accommodate up to 12 guests and depart from Puerto Banús, but they cater to different moods. The Mangusta 80 is a sporty 24-metre planing hull that delivers thrills and includes a free jet ski. The Ferretti 94 is a 29-metre flybridge cruiser built for lounging in style. Below we break down the differences so you can pick the right boat for your group.

Mangusta 80 vs Ferretti 94: Key specs at a glance

FeatureMangusta 80Ferretti 94
Length24 m29 m
Max guests1212
Min charter4 hoursOn request
Starting price (4h)€4,719On request
Jet ski includedYesNo
FlybridgeNoYes
DeparturePuerto BanúsPuerto Banús

All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and 21% IVA. See our full fleet for [other boats](/).

Speed and performance: Mangusta 80 takes the lead

The Mangusta 80 is built for speed. With its planing hull and powerful engines, it can reach around 32-34 knots, making it one of the faster options in its class. The Ferretti 94, while still capable of 28-30 knots, is heavier and designed for cruising comfort rather than outright pace. If your group wants to feel the wind and cover more coastline in a day — say, from Puerto Banús to Estepona or even Sotogrande — the Mangusta 80 is the better choice. The free jet ski adds another layer of adrenaline for water fun.

Space and luxury: Ferretti 94 wins on comfort

The Ferretti 94 is 5 metres longer and offers significantly more interior volume. Its flybridge provides an elevated sunbathing area with panoramic views of Marbella's coast, while the main saloon is spacious enough for a seated dinner or lounging in air conditioning. The Mangusta 80 has a more compact, open-plan layout that prioritises the aft deck and bow sunpads. For a relaxed day with elderly guests or those who prefer shade and comfort, the Ferretti 94 is the superior option. It's ideal for cruising towards Cabopino or Cala del Faro without rushing.

Which boat is better for a party?

It depends on the vibe. The Mangusta 80 with its jet ski and sporty atmosphere is perfect for an active group that wants to swim, speed, and party in style. The Ferretti 94 suits a more sophisticated gathering — think champagne on the flybridge, music from the onboard sound system, and a long, lazy lunch near Cala Cortés. Both boats can handle a party, but the Mangusta 80 leans towards fun, while the Ferretti 94 leans towards elegance.

Pricing and booking

The Mangusta 80 has a fixed starting price of €4,719 for 4 hours (including the jet ski). You can extend to 8 hours for a full day. The Ferretti 94 is priced on request — contact us via WhatsApp for a custom quote. Given the Ferretti's larger size and luxury features, expect a higher daily rate, but it may be worth it for the extra space. Both boats are popular, so book early, especially during July and August when Marbella's marina is busiest.

Where you'll cruise

Both depart from Puerto Banús, so you'll have access to the same stunning coastline. Popular routes include heading west towards the Golden Mile and Marbella Marina, or east to Cabopino and Cala del Faro. The Mangusta 80's speed means you can easily reach Sotogrande in about 40 minutes. The Ferretti 94 is better for a leisurely cruise to Cala Cortés or anchoring near Río Verde. Your skipper will tailor the itinerary to your group's preferences.

Final verdict

Choose the Mangusta 80 if you want speed, a jet ski, and a sporty day out. Choose the Ferretti 94 if space, luxury, and a flybridge matter more. Both deliver an unforgettable Marbella charter experience. For more help deciding, browse our [full fleet](/).
